title: Parties and status: agency worker on a contract for services
subject: agency

all.body:
These terms are between **{{parties.company_name}}** of {{parties.company_address}} ("the Company", "we", "us") and **{{parties.worker_name}}** of {{parties.worker_address}} ("you"). The Company is an employment business. It supplies you to work temporarily for its clients (each a "hirer"), under the hirer's supervision and direction. These terms start on {{engagement.start}}.

You are engaged under a contract for services. You are an agency worker and a worker, not an employee of the Company or of any hirer. You are not employed by a hirer just because you appear on its rota or staff list.

These terms are the terms of engagement required by regulations 14 and 15 of the Conduct of Employment Agencies and Employment Businesses Regulations 2003. Together with Schedule 1 (Key particulars) and the assignment details we give you for each assignment, they are also your written statement of particulars under section 1 of the Employment Rights Act 1996.

all.body:
We will try to find you suitable assignments, but we do not have to offer you any, and you do not have to accept any you are offered. Between assignments you are not paid, unless these terms say otherwise.

Before you start each assignment we will tell you the hirer's identity and business, the start date and likely length of the assignment, the role, type of work, location and hours, any health and safety risks the hirer knows about and the steps taken to control them, the experience, training, qualifications or licences needed, and any expenses. If we tell you any of this verbally, we will confirm it in writing as regulation 21 of the Conduct of Employment Agencies and Employment Businesses Regulations 2003 requires.

During an assignment the hirer supervises and directs your day-to-day work, and you must follow its reasonable instructions, site rules and assignment instructions as well as these terms. If you cannot attend a shift, or something on site worries you, tell us and the hirer as soon as you can.

title: No fees and freedom to work elsewhere
subject: agency

all.body:
We will not charge you a fee for finding or trying to find you work, as section 6 of the Employment Agencies Act 1973 and the Conduct of Employment Agencies and Employment Businesses Regulations 2003 provide. Using any optional service we offer is never a condition of finding you work.

You may work for others, and you may take up a direct job with a hirer. We will not penalise you, or threaten to, because you do. Any fee for that move is a matter between us and the hirer, and you never pay it.

title: Your rights from the first day of an assignment
subject: agency

all.body:
From your first day on an assignment you have the right under regulations 12 and 13 of the Agency Workers Regulations 2010:

- to use the hirer's shared facilities and amenities, such as a canteen, rest room, drinks facilities, car parking or transport between sites, on the same basis as the hirer's own staff, unless there is an objective reason not to; and
- to be told about relevant job vacancies with the hirer, so that you have the same chance as its own staff to apply for a permanent job.

If you are refused either of these, tell us and we will raise it with the hirer.

title: Equal treatment after the qualifying period
subject: agency

all.body:
After the statutory qualifying period of 12 continuous calendar weeks in the same role with the same hirer, you are entitled under the Agency Workers Regulations 2010 to the same basic working and employment conditions as if the hirer had recruited you directly into that role. These cover pay, working time, night work, rest breaks and rest periods, and annual leave.

Under the statutory rules some breaks pause the qualifying period rather than restart it, for example short gaps between assignments, sickness, holiday and some family leave, and some periods count towards it. A new role that is substantively different, or a gap longer than the statutory limit, starts a new qualifying period. We keep a record of your assignment weeks with each hirer.

Before each assignment, and when you complete the qualifying period, we ask the hirer for the information we need about its comparable directly recruited staff. You may ask us in writing for information about your basic working and employment conditions, and we will reply within the statutory time limit. After the qualifying period you are also entitled to paid time off for antenatal appointments.

title: Ending an assignment or these terms
subject: agency

all.body:
You or we may end an assignment, or these terms, at any time. You must give us {{notice.worker}} notice, and we will give you {{notice.company}} notice, or the statutory minimum notice in section 86 of the Employment Rights Act 1996 if you are our employee and that is longer. A hirer may also ask us to end an assignment early.

These terms continue between assignments until one of us ends them in writing. When they end, we will pay you everything you have earned, including any holiday pay due, and you must return any passes, keys, uniform or equipment.

This document is from **{{parties.company_name}}** of {{parties.company_address}} ("the Company", "we", "us") to **{{parties.worker_name}}** ("you"). You are supplied to us by **{{agency.name}}** ("your agency") to work on a temporary assignment as {{hirer.role}}, starting on {{hirer.start}}, at {{hirer.location}}. You report to {{hirer.reports_to}}.

**This is not a contract of employment, and it does not make you our employee or worker.** Your terms of engagement are with your agency. Your agency (or an umbrella company it uses) pays you and deals with your tax, holiday pay and pension. Being on our rota, staff list or systems does not change that. If we ever offer you a direct job, it will be in a separate written contract.

This document explains the rights you have while you work with us under the Agency Workers Regulations 2010, and records the site rules you agree to follow while you are on assignment with us.
